newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit recovers slightly from mid-session low.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit recovers slightly from mid-session low.

text.p: The ringgit recovered partially from mid-session lows on mild dollar selling from Kuala Lumpur-based banks, but movement was expected to be limited by small volumes, dealers said on Monday.
They said Malaysian banks were playing the range, backed by genuine commercial demand for dollars as well as ringgit.
"Morning, there was some commercial buying by KL banks. But, there was selling around 2.5260 level," a dealer with a Malaysian bank in Kuala Lumpur said.
He said dollar selling was partly due to a large syndicated dollar loan being gradually converted to ringgit.
The dealer said dollar/ringgit was expected to trade in a 2.5220/5300 range this week.
Other dealers said ringgit's movement was largely in line with the movement in dollar/majors.
They said October trade data was expected to influence trading in the near-term, though the absence of many players ahead of the year-end would reduce movement and volumes.
They said the market was divided over whether Malaysia would report a surplus or deficit after three months of surpluses.
At 0800 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5257/62 a dollar after hitting a mid-session low of 2.5270.
